name: Somalia
summary: Formed in 1960 from British and Italian Somaliland; the state collapsed in 1991 and is being rebuilt; Somaliland in the north acts as independent.

knownFor.label: Hawala
knownFor.note: Money-transfer networks used by Somalis worldwide.

location.value: The Horn of Africa, with Africa’s longest mainland coastline.

terrain.value: Plateaus, plains and highlands, with rugged mountain ranges in the far north.

climate.value: Hot all year, with monsoon winds and irregular rainfall; semi-arid.

resources.value: Livestock (the world’s largest camel population) and rich fishing grounds.

disasters.value: Severe droughts; in 2026 the UN warned that six million people faced food crises.

population.value: Over 19 million, of whom about 2.7 million live in Mogadishu.

urbanisation.value: Mogadishu is the capital and largest city; about 55% of people lived in towns in 2024.

migration.value: A large diaspora sends remittances of about US$1 billion a year.

economicBase.value: An informal economy based mainly on livestock, remittances from Somalis abroad, and telecommunications.

tradeRoutes.value: Ports such as Mogadishu, Bosaso, Berbera, Kismayo and Merca.

wealth.value: Among the least developed countries in the world.

moneyAndTax.value: The Somali shilling; the US dollar is also widely used.

inequality.value: Large gaps between the capital and rural areas.

keyRulers.value: Aden Abdullah Osman Daar (first president, 1960). Siad Barre (seized power in 1969).

institutions.value: A two-house Federal Parliament; the federal government was formed under the 2012 provisional constitution.

stability.value: The government collapsed in 1991 at the start of the civil war; insurgents such as al-Shabaab still control much of the centre and south.

eliteConflict.value: Competition between political parties and leaders.

armyAndTech.value: The Somali Armed Forces, rebuilt since 2004, supported by African Union peacekeepers.

majorWars.value: The Ogaden War with Ethiopia (from 1977) and the Somali Civil War (from 1991).

territoryChange.value: The north declared independence as the Republic of Somaliland in 1991; no foreign government recognised it until Israel did in 2025.

inventions.value: No major inventions are associated with the modern state.

scienceEducation.value: A literacy campaign under the revolutionary government raised literacy to 70%, then one of the highest in Africa.

openness.value: Open to trade and foreign investment, with periods of restriction.

communicationTransport.value: Mobile phone companies let customers transfer money and bank by phone.

religion.value: Almost everyone is a Sunni Muslim; Islam is the state religion.

artsArchitecture.value: A strong poetry tradition; Somalia has been called a “Nation of Poets”.

socialStructure.value: About 85% are ethnic Somalis, traditionally organised into nomadic pastoral clans.

sharedIdentity.value: Shared Somali ethnicity, the Somali language and Islam.

dailyLife.value: About 80% are nomadic or semi-nomadic herders of goats, sheep, camels and cattle.

ideasReligions.value: Sunni Islam, with many Sufi orders.

colonisation.value: Colonised by Italy and Britain in the late 19th century until 1960.

overallCertainty.value: Basic facts are well documented; some figures are estimates.
